Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for taking our RFP. As we consolidate vendor responses, a few targeted questions came up from our identity and security teams on admin segregation and provisioning controls. Could you confirm the following at a high level and attach any concise examples: 

1) Delegated admin model — can you describe how tenant-level admins are scoped vs org-level superadmins, and whether RBAC roles can be restricted by tenant/idp?

2) SCIM filtering and attribute transforms — do you support SCIM filter expressions or attribute mapping on per-connector basis? We have multiple IdPs and need group membership filtered into different Redwood tenants.

3) SAML/OIDC mapping — do you support configurable attribute maps (email, groups, role claim) and fallback rules when claims are missing?

4) Auditability — token/session lifecycle logs, admin actions (who changed role X for tenant Y) and export options (CSV/JSON).

We prefer short examples or a single spreadsheet you can share. Procurement would like this back by EOD Wednesday (2026-05-19) if possible.

Best,

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. I pulled together a short control matrix and two small examples that map directly to your four points. High level answers below, and I attached the spreadsheets/snippets for your architecture and procurement teams. If you want, we can walk through them in a 30-min call.

1) Delegated admin model
- Redwood supports a two-tier admin model: organization-level Superadmins (can manage global billing, deployment routing, and create/destroy tenants) and Tenant Admins (scoped to a specific tenant or VPC).
- RBAC is role-based and attribute-aware: roles can be scoped by tenant_id and, optionally, constrained by IdP-backed group membership. You can create custom roles limited to specific APIs (e.g., embeddings-only) and to tenant contexts.

2) SCIM filtering & transforms
- We support per-connector SCIM attribute mapping and pre-provisioning filters. Filters use a subset of SCIM filter syntax; common patterns supported: group eq "X", userName sw "svc-".
- We also support attribute transforms (rename, concat, default) so you can map external group claims into internal role tags. See scim-filtering-examples.json attached.

3) SAML / OIDC mapping and fallbacks
- Attribute mapping UI enables you to set primary claim paths, fallbacks, and default values when claims are missing. Role claims can be sourced from SAML attributes or OIDC token claims (roles, groups).
- For OIDC, we support custom claim names and JSONPath extraction for complex nested claims.

4) Auditability
- Admin actions (role/grant changes, tenant assignment, service config edits) are logged with actor, timestamp, and affected entity.
- Session/token lifecycle events (issue, refresh, revoke) are retained for 90 days by default in Hosted; longer retention is available for Dedicated/Private with configurable exports. Logs can be exported via the Console as CSV/JSON or streamed to your SIEM via our audit webhook.

Attachments: control matrix (redwood_admin-guardrails-control-matrix.xlsx), examples (scim-filtering-examples.json, saml-attribute-mapping-sample.txt)

Let me know the best time for a 30-min walkthrough and if you'd like the team to produce a sample tenant-level policy for one of your IdPs.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Architect, Identity & Security
Redwood Inference

I also attached a simple mapping diagram (in the control matrix workbook, Sheet 2) that shows SAML/OIDC claim -> internal role mapping examples.

Summary of changes: 
- MFA enforcement: Superadmins require MFA by default; tenant admins can be required via tenant policy. We recommend IdP-enforced MFA for all admin users.
- Retention: Hosted audit logs default 90 days; Dedicated customers can get 1yr or longer via retention add-on; Private supports customer-defined retention and local archival. Exports to SIEM available for all tiers.
- SCIM note: Filters are evaluated at connector ingest; we include examples for group-based filtering and regex-based userName filters.
